content: Chimaphila umbellata, commonly known as Umbellate Wintergreen, Pipsissewa, or Prince's Pine, is a small, perennial flowering plant that thrives in dry woodlands or sandy soils. It is native to the cool temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. The plant typically grows to a height of 10 to 35 cm and features evergreen, shiny, bright green leaves. These leaves are arranged in opposite pairs or in whorls of three to four along the stem. The margins of the leaves are shallowly toothed, with fine hairs present at the tips of the teeth. The flowers of Chimaphila umbellata are either white or pink and are grouped in small umbels, each containing four to eight flowers. Despite having green leaves throughout the year, Chimaphila umbellata derives a significant portion of its nutrition from soil fungi, making it a partial myco-heterotroph. This characteristic is consistent with other related plants, such as those in the Pyrola genus, which are known to be either partial or full myco-heterotrophs. The species is taxonomically divided into four subspecies based on geographic distribution: Chimaphila umbellata subsp. umbellata is found in Europe and Asia. Chimaphila umbellata subsp. acuta is native to southwestern North America. Chimaphila umbellata subsp. cisatlantica is located in northeastern North America. Chimaphila umbellata subsp. occidentalis is distributed in northwestern North America. Chimaphila umbellata has practical applications, particularly as a flavoring agent in candies and soft drinks, including root beer. The name Pipsissewa originates from the Cree language and translates to It-breaks-into-small-pieces. Additionally, the name Pipsissewa is used for a character in the Uncle Wiggly series of books authored by Howard R. Garis.
